To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
anti-idiotypic antibodies in pooled normal human IgG, following depletion of autoantibodies, have the ability to recognize and bind directly to anti-DNase IgG and inhibit its binding to DNA.
antiidiotypes in IVIG can inhibit anti-DNA activity in lupus sera and that these antiidiotypics may be useful in the treatment of SLE.
the antiidiotypes of intravenous immune globulins are directed against anti-DNA, and that they can be used as therapeutic agents to treat patients with autoimmune diseases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection and purification of antiidiotype antibodies against anti-DNA, which are expressed in pooled normal human IgG after depletion of anti-DNase, anti-Fc and anti-F(ab)’2.
the development of a novel method for the isolation of antiidiotypes from normal IgG.
the purification of a monoclonal antibody (MAb) that recognizes the idiotypic specificity of anti-DNA antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of intravenous immune globulins is a safe and effective treatment in patients with primary immunodeficiency disorders.
the antiidiotypes present in intravenous immune gammaglobulin (IVIG) have a direct effect in the inhibition of anti-dsDNA antibody in systemic lupus erythematosus.
antiidiotypics in pooled normal IgG are capable of inhibiting the binding of anti-DNA to DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
antiidiotypics are not the only mechanism for the beneficial effects of IVIG in autoimmune diseases.
we were the first to show that antiidiotypes against anti-DNA were in pooled normal IgG and that these could be purified and shown to have the properties of antiidiotypes.

the antiidiotypes in normal human immunoglobulin (IgG) may have a therapeutic role in autoimmune diseases, and the antiidiotyping process may be a general mechanism of action for intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) in autoimmune disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-idiotypes in the IVIg are directed against the idiotypes of the autoantibodies, and not against the autoantigens.
we have identified a novel mechanism of immune regulation in autoimmune disease.
we have shown for the first time the existence of anti-anti-DNA idiotypes in the normal population.
